summary: Beiho Takashima (1875–1949) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at and held a post at Toyo University. He also founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.

Bela Bhattacharya (born 1950) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and later as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Bemé Shyi Drol was a scholar who pursued studies under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Melvyn C. Goldstein. He later served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who completed her PhD at SOAS. She held posts at UC Berkeley (~2013–2014), the University of Virginia (~2014–2017), and the University of Bristol (~2017).

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at institutions including the University of Calcutta and the University of London (D.Litt.). He taught at the University of Calcutta as Lektor (1913–1914) and Professor (1918–1948).

Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a sinologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held major appointments at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University (2002).

Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied with Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Stanford (~2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. He was an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2009–2016).

Benjamin C. Ray (born 1940) is a religious studies scholar. He held a long career at the University of Virginia, including an appointment as Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in Religious Studies (attested 2000 and 2026).
Benjamin Fleming is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).
Benjamin Goldstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As of 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Benjamin Lewis Rice (1837–1927) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as head and Director of the Department of Public Instruction in Mysore (~1868–1883) and Director of the Karnataka State Archaeology Department (~1884–1889).
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Yale University (~1985–1989) and Harvard University (~1991–1996). He held a post at the University of Michigan (~2004).

Benjamin Wood is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett. He also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Taisho University (1926) and head of both Sanko Library and Sanko Research Institute (~1948–1971).

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Calcutta and Dhaka universities. He served as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1927) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1927–1952).

Benoît Vermander (born 1960) is a sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) before joining Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who earned a Doctorat d'État in Paris. He held major professorships at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).
